title: World Championship Decks 2003: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: It's hard to be humble when the whole world is bite-size.
Webs of illusion unravel in the light of truth.
Some tides need no moon.
It teaches *you* to play dead.
"The specimen seems to be broken."
"What you made will be unmade. What you learned will be unlearned. And when you're done, you will be undone." —Ambassador Laquatus
Just because your eyes are open doesn't mean you're awake.
"The best foresight is hindsight." —Empress Llawan
"The awestruck birds gazed at Wonder. Slowly, timidly, they rose into the air." —*Scroll of Beginnings*
Books are like crops—they must be thinned for best yield.
The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy.
It's so tough it can frighten itself into hiding.
The land drank power from the Mirari as though it had thirsted forever.
Teroh dreams of his enemies' doom.
"It offers you what you want, not what you need." —Braids, dementia summoner
The elfhames are the closest thing to "civilization" the elves allow themselves.
From Otaria, the sun above meets the sea below at a glittering horizon.
He wished for knowledge, but not for the will to apply it.
The scrape of shovels and the tumble of cold dirt soon muffled their pleas.
"Sheesh! How am I supposed to make a decent living around here?" —Cabal grave robber
A grave is the safest place to store ill-gotten treasures.
"His sacrifice shall not be forgotten. Now toss his body over there with the others." —Phage the Untouchable
Zombies mourn for the living and celebrate those who will soon be given the gift of death.
You are who you eat.
"The first birth celebrates life. The second birth mocks it." —Mystic elder
"My eyes are my strongest feature."
"Pound the steel until it fits. Doesn't work? Bash to bits." —Dwarven forging song
"When the air burns, only death breathes deep." —Bogardan mage
The insects keep the wurm's hide free from parasites. In return, the wurm doesn't eat the insects.
The pits have their own form of mercy.
He has journeyed where none have been before. Now he returns to ensure that none follow.
"For its time as a mortal, Anger chose a shell of boiling rock." —*Scroll of Beginnings*
She wished for a weapon, but not for the skill to wield it.
The Patriarch dreams of vile plague.
Daru soldiers learned it's better to have a clean death from a sharp blade than to tangle with a goblin's rusted chains.
"Ha, banishment? Be merciful, say 'death,' For exile hath more terror in his look, Much more than death." —William Shakespeare, *Romeo and Juliet*
"Family plots are so convenient." —Cabal Patriarch
"I can't hear them scream, but at least I don't have to listen to them beg." —Phage the Untouchable
Throw enough goblins at any problem and it should go away. At the very least, there'll be fewer goblins.
"Let's play 'sled.' Here's how it works: you're the sled."
For some reason, goblin fighting school isn't as crowded on day two.
"I like goblins. They make funny little popping sounds when they die." —Braids, dementia summoner
"If it didn't hurt, how would I know it worked?"
The carnage of conflicts long past still stains the Otarian soil.
Pardic barbarians didn't complain when the Order started blaming every crisis on the Cabal.
"I don't rub salt in wounds. I use sulfur." —Matoc, lavamancer
They poured from the Skirk Ridge like lava, burning and devouring everything in their path.
